recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No source follow-up is needed for FHIR-7626 unless a future work group decision changes ContactPoint.rank semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-7626 was a Published FHIR-core datatypes change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking that ContactPoint provide a rank attribute so communication modalities could be tried in preference order. The final record endorsed the change based on PA support and expected a positive integer.
initial_application: The historical source application is git commit d45b815efc6c29cd65295e44bf82863887c82875, subject '#7626 - add ContactPoint.rank'. Current source/datatypes/contactpoint.xml still defines ContactPoint.rank with cardinality 0..1 and type positiveInt.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists ContactPoint as an active datatype and marks it normative. Later published issues FHIR-16984 and FHIR-38824 clarified ranking semantics without removing the element: lower rank values are more preferred, rank need not follow array order, ranks need not be unique or sequential, and not every repetition must carry a rank. A quoted FHIR-7626 Zulip/Confluence search found no conflicting community decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit and made no source changes because the current authoritative ContactPoint spreadsheet already satisfies FHIR-7626 and incorporates later approved clarifications.

related_jiras.note: Published clarification that ContactPoints with lower rank values are more preferred than those with higher rank values, avoiding an implication that array order controls ranking.
Published clarification that ranks need not be unique or sequential and that some repetitions can be unranked.
